author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: I need the nightly data pipeline to run on its own, from ingestion through to validation. Right now, the manual checks are a bottleneck that keeps pushing the forecast job past the morning order window. I want an automated validation layer that catches bad data instantly, so the system can self correct without waiting for a human to spot the error. The more automated this stretch is, the better, because it removes the human delay entirely. I am not asking for a partial fix. I want the whole process to be automated so the forecast job starts on time every single night, giving store managers the reliable data they need before they open the app.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that 'the more automated this stretch is, the better' and that they are not asking for a partial fix, indicating that exceeding the minimum requirement of full automation would make them happier by completely removing human delay.
